Section 4 • \(\xi\)3D

4.1 Per-sample (realization-level) 3D two-point correlation, \(\widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{r}_{\perp},\Delta\right)\)

Given one realization \(s\), consider the fractional fluctuation fields \(\delta_i^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda)\) and \(\delta_j^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda)\) on a set of sightlines covering a transverse domain \(\mathcal{A}_\perp\) and the spectral interval \([\Lambda_a,\Lambda_b]\) of length \(L_\Lambda\). The per-sample 3D two-point (cross) correlation function correlates the two fields on two sightlines separated by the transverse lag \(\vec{r}_{\perp}\), at the spectral lag \(\Delta\), and averages over all the positions for which both points lie inside the available domain. With the window \begin{equation} W_{\vec{r}_{\perp},\Delta}(\vec{x}_\perp,\Lambda) \equiv \mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{A}_\perp}\!\left(\vec{x}_\perp+\vec{r}_{\perp}\right)\, \mathbf{1}_{[\Lambda_a,\Lambda_b]}\!\left(\Lambda+\Delta\right), \tag{4.1} \end{equation} we define (without periodic wrap) \begin{equation} \widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{r}_{\perp},\Delta\right) \equiv \frac{ \int_{\mathcal{A}_\perp}\! d^2x_\perp \int_{\Lambda_a}^{\Lambda_b}\! d\Lambda\; W_{\vec{r}_{\perp},\Delta}(\vec{x}_\perp,\Lambda)\, \delta_i^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda\right)\, \delta_j^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp}+\vec{r}_{\perp},\Lambda+\Delta\right) }{ \int_{\mathcal{A}_\perp}\! d^2x_\perp \int_{\Lambda_a}^{\Lambda_b}\! d\Lambda\; W_{\vec{r}_{\perp},\Delta}(\vec{x}_\perp,\Lambda) }, \qquad |\Delta| < L_\Lambda. \tag{4.2} \end{equation} The denominator is \(\left|\mathcal{A}_\perp(\vec{r}_{\perp})\right|\,(L_\Lambda-|\Delta|)\), with \(\left|\mathcal{A}_\perp(\vec{r}_{\perp})\right|\) the area of the part of \(\mathcal{A}_\perp\) whose shift by \(\vec{r}_{\perp}\) remains inside \(\mathcal{A}_\perp\) (the whole area \(|\mathcal{A}_\perp|\) for a transverse domain with periodic boundaries). The geometry of a pair and the window are sketched in Figs. 6 and 7.

Exchanging the two points of every pair gives, for real-valued fields,2 \begin{equation} \widehat{\xi}_{ji}^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{r}_{\perp},\Delta\right) = \widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s)}\!\left(-\vec{r}_{\perp},-\Delta\right). \tag{4.3} \end{equation} This is an exact identity for every realization, but it requires flipping both components of the lag at once. Flipping them separately gives different statements:

  • Transverse flip, \(\vec{r}_{\perp}\to-\vec{r}_{\perp}\) at fixed \(\Delta\): it is not an identity of the per-sample estimator, since \(\widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s)}(\vec{r}_{\perp},\Delta)\) and \(\widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s)}(-\vec{r}_{\perp},\Delta)\) are built from different pairs of points. It holds for the ensemble 2PCF under isotropy around the line of sight (a rotation by \(\pi\) of the transverse plane), \(\xi_{ij}(-\vec{r}_{\perp},\Delta)=\xi_{ij}(\vec{r}_{\perp},\Delta)\), and therefore for the per-sample estimator only on average. Combined with Eq. (4.3), it gives \(\xi_{ji}(\vec{r}_{\perp},\Delta)=\xi_{ij}(\vec{r}_{\perp},-\Delta)\).

  • Line-of-sight flip, \(\Delta\to-\Delta\) at fixed \(\vec{r}_{\perp}\): it does not hold in general, not even for the ensemble, because the line of sight is a special direction. For a cross-correlation (\(i\neq j\)), the sign of \(\Delta\) distinguishes which of the two fields lies ahead (e.g. when the two lines are offset in the spectral coordinate), so \(\xi_{ij}(\vec{r}_{\perp},-\Delta)\neq\xi_{ij}(\vec{r}_{\perp},\Delta)\). For an autocorrelation (\(i=j\)), the previous item gives \(\xi_{ii}(\vec{r}_{\perp},-\Delta)=\xi_{ii}(\vec{r}_{\perp},\Delta)\) for the ensemble, again only under isotropy around the line of sight.

2

In the numerator of Eq. (4.2) for \(\widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s)}(-\vec{r}_{\perp},-\Delta)\), the integration runs over \(\vec{x}_\perp,\vec{x}_\perp-\vec{r}_{\perp}\in\mathcal{A}_\perp\) and \(\Lambda,\Lambda-\Delta\in[\Lambda_a,\Lambda_b]\), with integrand \(\delta_i^{(s)}(\vec{x}_\perp,\Lambda)\,\delta_j^{(s)}(\vec{x}_\perp-\vec{r}_{\perp},\Lambda-\Delta)\). The change of variables \(\vec{x}_\perp\to\vec{x}_\perp+\vec{r}_{\perp}\), \(\Lambda\to\Lambda+\Delta\) (unit Jacobian) maps the domain onto \(\vec{x}_\perp,\vec{x}_\perp+\vec{r}_{\perp}\in\mathcal{A}_\perp\), \(\Lambda,\Lambda+\Delta\in[\Lambda_a,\Lambda_b]\), i.e. that of \(W_{\vec{r}_{\perp},\Delta}\), and the integrand onto \(\delta_j^{(s)}(\vec{x}_\perp,\Lambda)\,\delta_i^{(s)}(\vec{x}_\perp+\vec{r}_{\perp},\Lambda+\Delta)\), the numerator of \(\widehat{\xi}_{ji}^{(s)}(\vec{r}_{\perp},\Delta)\). The denominators coincide by the same change of variables.
